questions.prompt: 1. Ziad wants to do an experiment with water and a glass tube. Which room should he go to?
questions.evidence: Experiments belong in the laboratory. The library is for books and the playground is for play.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Naming school rooms and their use

questions.prompt: 2. Choose True or False: if the music room is on the right of the art room, then the art room is on the left of the music room.
questions.evidence: Right and left are opposites, so the same two rooms seen the other way round give the opposite sentence. The statement is true.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Describing where a room is

questions.prompt: 3. Read the description of Nadia’s school. Which rooms are on the upper floor?
questions.evidence: The text puts the classrooms and the computer room on the upper floor and the library and laboratory on the ground floor.
options: a) the library and the laboratory
b) the classrooms and the computer room
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading where rooms are in a school description

questions.prompt: 4. Read the description of Nadia’s school again. Choose True or False: the library is upstairs.
questions.evidence: The first sentence puts the library on the ground floor, so the statement is false.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading where rooms are in a school description

questions.prompt: 5. Read Rami’s week. On which day has Rami got Art?
questions.evidence: The third sentence says Rami has got Art on Tuesday.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a simple weekly subject table

questions.prompt: 6. Read Rami’s week again. Which two subjects has Rami got together on Monday?
questions.evidence: The second sentence names English and Maths together on Monday.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a simple weekly subject table

questions.prompt: 7. Read Rami’s week again. Choose True or False: Rami’s favourite subject is Science.
questions.evidence: The text says his favourite subject is Art, and gives drawing as the reason.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a simple weekly subject table

questions.prompt: 8. Read Rami’s week again. Write the day when Rami has got English.
questions.evidence: English appears in the sentence about Monday, together with Maths.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using the days of the week with subjects

questions.prompt: 9. Layla mixes red and blue paint to make purple. Which subject is she working in?
questions.evidence: Mixing paints is drawing and painting work, which belongs to Art.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Matching a subject to what pupils do in it

questions.prompt: 10. A pupil writes 23, 24, 25 on the board. Which number comes next?
questions.evidence: Counting on one from twenty-five gives twenty-six; twenty-seven would skip a number.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Continuing a number pattern up to fifty

questions.prompt: 11. Which numeral matches the number word forty-nine?
questions.evidence: Forty-nine is four tens and nine ones, written 49. 94 is ninety-four.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Matching a numeral to its word

questions.prompt: 12. Write the number word for 30.
questions.evidence: The tens words are ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, so 30 is thirty.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing number words

questions.prompt: 13. Which word contains the two letters oa?
questions.evidence: Goat is spelled g-o-a-t. Broom has oo and house has ou.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising the revision letter pairs

questions.prompt: 14. Which word contains the two letters ou?
questions.evidence: Mouse is spelled m-o-u-s-e. Meat has ea and coat has oa.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising the revision letter pairs

questions.prompt: 15. Build the food word: m + ea + t. Write the whole word.
questions.evidence: Joining m, ea and t makes meat, the ea word printed in the revision page.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Building words from printed letter pairs

questions.prompt: 16. A broom is used for sweeping the floor. Which letter pair do you hear in the middle of broom?
questions.evidence: Broom is spelled b-r-o-o-m, so the middle letters are oo.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising the revision letter pairs

questions.prompt: 17. You want to know which subject your new friend likes best. Which question should you ask?
questions.evidence: Only the second question asks about a favourite subject. The others ask about a place and about brothers.
options: b) What is your favourite subject?
c) How many brothers have you got?
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking about a friend’s school life

questions.prompt: 18. Choose True or False: a flat is a home where a family can live, and it can be upstairs in a building.
questions.evidence: A flat is a set of rooms to live in, and flats are often on an upper floor, so the statement is true.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Talking about where a family lives

questions.prompt: 19. Huda has got two sisters and one brother. How many brothers has Huda got?
questions.evidence: Only the brothers are asked about, and the sentence gives one brother.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Talking about brothers and sisters

questions.prompt: 20. Write a sentence beginning with I. Use all four words exactly once: English / got / I / have.
questions.evidence: Beginning with I, the order is I + have + got + English, which names a subject the pupil has.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing a clear English sentence about school
